title: The 'snake charmer' nickname and learning slap tongue
summary: The snake charmer name lasted as long as he was in New Orleans; he learned slap tongue from Louie Warnecke in Piron's band, became the King of the Slap Tongue and took revenge by not showing up for jobs.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: How long did the nickname "snake charmer" stick with you? Because you mentioned it on the other tape in a different context.
Yeah. Oh, that lasted a long time.
As long as I was in New Orleans.
But, you know, when I got the sax then I learned how to what they call "slap tongue." You see, in Piron's big band
he had an alto player called Louie Warnecke and he was the first one I ever heard do that slap tongue business.

You pop the reed; instead of making a noise, you have "pop," just like you pop, like you slap anything flat, you know. And so he taught me and I kept practicing at it, practicing. Then they called me the "King of the Slap Tongue." Then I got more work than I could ever handle. And all the guys that fired me and did me dirt, I says, "I'll get even with them." I'd take the job and I wouldn't go on it.
I had a lot of fun.
So you had another nickname, the "King of the Slap Tongue."
